title: Do the Benefits Outweigh the Risks of Hosting U.S. Military Bases?
gist: The teaser for a five-expert roundtable says the war with Iran has raised doubts among US host nations about retaliation risk and US reliability. It cites the sudden withdrawal of US B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford and Trump's pressure on allies; only the Japan view is partly visible and the rest is paywalled.

insights.claim: The war with Iran has raised questions in Arab Gulf states about whether hosting US installations exposes them to Iranian retaliation without providing sufficient protection.
insights.speaker: Ayumi Teraoka, Bruce Klingner, Anna Jacobs, Niklas Ebert, and Matthew Savill
insights.so_what: Host-nation political support for US basing in the Gulf is under pressure.

insights.claim: The sudden withdrawal of US B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in the UK earlier in October 2026, reportedly in response to an Iranian threat, highlighted the risks to host countries.
insights.speaker: Ayumi Teraoka, Bruce Klingner, Anna Jacobs, Niklas Ebert, and Matthew Savill
insights.so_what: Shows US posture can shift abruptly under threat, undermining host-country confidence.

insights.claim: The Trump administration's criticism of European countries, scaled-back exercises with South Korea and demand that Gulf states pay for protecting Hormuz shipping have not reinforced public support for hosting US sites.
insights.speaker: Ayumi Teraoka, Bruce Klingner, Anna Jacobs, Niklas Ebert, and Matthew Savill
insights.so_what: Alliance-cost politics could reduce US access and host financing over time.

insights.claim: Tokyo's concerns include inadequate US consultation before the Iran war despite exposing allies and bases to retaliation, and Washington's reluctance to defend partners.
insights.speaker: Ayumi Teraoka, Bruce Klingner, Anna Jacobs, Niklas Ebert, and Matthew Savill
insights.so_what: Japan's reliability doubts may speed its own defense buildup and hedging.

source_meta.author: Ayumi Teraoka, Bruce Klingner, Anna Jacobs, Niklas Ebert, and Matthew Savill
